extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, performers, and critics/scholars studying persona-based satire
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing and performing an ironic persona (the 'demeaning ditz') in stand-up/comedic performance: impersonating bigots to mock them while managing detectability and risk. Focuses on character construction, delivery, topic selection, and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear ironic persona
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear ironic persona? Mocks bigots by impersonating them. The persona is a character (named 'Sarah Silverman' in the example) who inhabits the performer's body — views expressed may not be shared by the real person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The persona must read as a role the performer is playing rather than the performer's genuine views. Signals that help: consistent character traits, stylized language/tone, contextual framing. Anti-pattern: persona indistinguishable from the performer's real-life stance, which increases risk of literal endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona delivering bigoted views to mock them
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the persona delivering bigoted views in order to mock those views? The technique involves a comic character endorsing bigoted views satirically/deadpan to subvert and expose absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the target of ridicule is the bigoted belief or system, not the oppressed group. Effective performances use endorsement-as-satire (deadpan) to reveal absurdity. Anti-pattern: targeting victims, endorsing bigotry without subversion, or ambiguous mockery that reads as praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony detectable to the intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the irony detectable to the intended audience? Success requires that the audience 'see through' the persona and hold the irony rather than take statements at face value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gauge audience sophistication and provide sufficient cues (tone, setup, contradictions) so intended viewers recognize satire. Scoring note: a joke that lands with intended viewers but not with the broader/less-aware audience may still be effective in context, but carries dissemination risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for misreading by the wrong audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the joke be misread by the wrong audience? The technique fails when audience members agree with the bigoted line on its face or when, without irony markers, jokes are repurposed as genuine statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess likelihood that parts of the audience will take lines literally. Mitigations: clearer framing, stronger character cues, or avoiding material that can be easily excerpted and shared without context. Anti-pattern: relying on subtle irony when the material is likely to reach audiences lacking contextual cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals something true about the targeted bigotry
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the technique reveal something true about the targeted bigotry? The aim is to subvert and expose the absurdity or truth underlying the bigoted stance, producing recognition or catharsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective pieces illuminate systemic or logical flaws in the target belief and create catharsis when audiences recognize the truth. If the performance only repeats hateful language without insight, it fails this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona proximity to performer identity (insulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: How distinct is the persona from the performer's real identity? The risk profile notes that Silverman 'doesn't insulate herself with fictional characters' and the persona 'looks/sounds exactly like Silverman.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High proximity increases risk that satire will be interpreted as sincere. Consider creating more overtly fictionalized markers or distancing devices when necessary. Scoring note: closer proximity may be artistically compelling but raises ethical and reputational stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery tone and sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the delivery tone calibrated? The method often uses 'almost pathological sincerity' or a beaming, deadpan delivery while offending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sincerity/deadpan can sell the persona and sharpen the satire, but it must be balanced with cues that signal irony. Anti-pattern: excessive sincerity with no irony markers, which can lead to endorsement readings; conversely, over-signaling can blunt comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-defined character traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the persona have clear, exaggerated traits (e.g., self-absorbed, clueless racist, too dumb to understand the stupidity of her words)? Silverman's 'demeaning ditz' is described as 'ignorant and arrogant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define traits that make the caricature recognizable and allow the audience to infer satire. Vague or inconsistent characterization makes the persona harder to read and increases misinterpretation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic appropriateness and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the topics chosen appropriate for this technique? Typical topics include racism, sexism, homophobia, politics, religion, white privilege, post-feminism, and trivialization of serious events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the heightened sensitivity of these subjects. Ensure the satire clearly targets oppressive ideas/power structures rather than trivializing victims' suffering. Anti-pattern: trivialization without clear critical intent; topic selection should consider audience and potential harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual vulnerability and repurposing risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the material vulnerable to being taken out of context or repurposed? The notes warn that out of context the material can be 'devastating' and 'repurposed' absent irony markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how clips, quotes, or social-media excerpts could be shared without context. Use stronger setup, repeatable irony cues, or avoid produce-able soundbites that strip critical framing. Scoring note: material that works live but is easily weaponized online scores poorly on this dimension.
